name: Skinvive

lead: Skinvive (Juvederm Volite) is an Allergan hyaluronic acid injectable placed in many tiny droplets within the skin itself. People choose it for a hydrated, glassy glow and finer texture rather than added volume.

Hyaluronic acid binds water, so skin can look plumper, more hydrated and smoother. Published evidence is small and recent, including a 2025 split-face trial of combined botulinum toxin and Skinvive and several manufacturer-linked registered trials, one of them on neck lines.

paras: A clinician injects it across the cheeks or other areas in a single session of microdroplets. People often repeat it a few times a year and combine it with other skin treatments or neurotoxin.
Filler injections can cause redness, swelling and bruising, and less commonly granulomas. It is clinician-administered.

web.title: SKINVIVE by JUVEDERM Receives U.S. FDA Approval (AbbVie)

angle.text: Skinvive is used for a hydrated, glassy glow and smoother texture rather than added volume. Hyaluronic acid placed in microdroplets within the skin binds water, so skin looks plumper and finer-textured. Evidence so far is early, from recent small trials.

lead: Skinvive (Juvederm Volite VYC-12) is a hyaluronic acid injectable made by Allergan that is placed in the skin itself in many small microdroplets to improve skin quality, rather than to add volume.[1][2] People use it to make skin look smoother, more hydrated and glowing, and to soften fine lines, without changing facial shape. It belongs to the Juvederm range of hyaluronic acid products.[3]

The manufacturer's site describes it as the first and only hyaluronic acid microdroplet injectable indicated to improve cheek skin smoothness, as an intradermal injection in adults over 21, available only through a licensed physician or practitioner, with results lasting about six months with optimal treatment.[4]
Evidence found is limited to a 2025 split-face trial of combined botulinum toxin and Skinvive and a handful of manufacturer-linked registered trials, including one of Volite for neck lines.

paras: Hyaluronic acid is a substance found naturally in skin, muscles and tendons, and cross-linked forms in fillers last longer than natural hyaluronic acid, which is metabolised in about half a day; the body absorbs Juvederm filler usually within six to nine months.[3] Skinvive is the product name for Juvederm Volite VYC-12 in the study literature.[1]

Unlike volumising fillers that are injected deeper to lift or contour, microdroplet products are deposited within the skin in many small amounts. Wikipedia's Juvederm article says hyaluronic acid can absorb up to 1,000 times its weight in water, which is the basis for descriptions of its hydrating effect.[3]

Wikipedia traces hyaluronic acid research to 1934, when Karl Meyer and John Palmer of Columbia University isolated it from a cow's eye and showed it helps maintain skin volume and hydration; it was used in medicine by the 1990s and for facial augmentation in Europe in 1996.[3] The Juvederm filler was approved by the US FDA in June 2006, on the basis of a US study of 146 subjects comparing it with a bovine collagen filler over 24 weeks, in which 88 percent of subjects preferred the Juvederm-treated fold.[3]

Skinvive is the microdroplet product in the Juvederm range, marketed for skin smoothness rather than fold correction. Its manufacturer lists a US indication of improving cheek skin smoothness in adults over 21.[4]

Allergan Aesthetics, an AbbVie company, announced US FDA approval of Skinvive by Juvederm on 15 May 2023, describing it as the first and only hyaluronic acid intradermal microdroplet injection approved for skin smoothness in the US, indicated to improve cheek skin smoothness in adults over 21 across Fitzpatrick skin types I to VI.[5] The release says the FDA requires providers to complete a training programme before purchasing or administering it.[5] It names Macrene Alexiades as lead investigator, and quotes her as saying the product is "truly innovative because it works beneath the skin's surface" to increase hydration.[5]

In the manufacturer's randomised, multicentre, evaluator-blinded pivotal trial, as reported in the approval announcement, 58 percent (73 of 125) of treated patients improved by at least one point on the Allergan Cheek Smoothness Scale at one month and 56 percent (69 of 124) at six months.[5] The company also reported patient-satisfaction results at six months versus before treatment: 72 percent for hydration (24 percent before), 83 percent for healthy-looking skin (38 percent), 63 percent for radiance (11 percent) and 69 percent for feeling refreshed (16 percent).[5] These figures come from the manufacturer's release rather than a peer-reviewed paper.

The research found is small and recent. A 2025 randomised, double-blind split-face trial in 25 women with moderate to severe canthal lines (Merz scale II to IV) gave all participants botulinum toxin and randomised each side of the face to receive Skinvive or a simulated injection, assessing electromyography, the Merz crow's-feet scale and FACE-Q appraisal at several time points.[1] Registered studies are examining microdroplet hyaluronic acid on skin quality in people using GLP-1 agonists and satisfaction after jawline and neck treatment.[6][7]

In the 2025 split-face trial, electromyography activity did not differ between sides at any time point (p = 0.86), but the side that also received Skinvive had lower crow's-feet severity at rest at 3 months (p = 0.04) and in contraction at 3 months (p = 0.007) and 6 months (p = 0.001); satisfaction was also higher on the combined side at 3 and 6 months (p = 0.001 for each).[1] The authors concluded that combining onabotulinumtoxinA with the hyaluronic acid could enhance improvement of canthal wrinkles.[1]

Skinvive sits within the trend toward 'skin booster' injectables, which is also a category in which other hyaluronic acid products are used outside the Juvederm line. Allergan has also run studies of combined treatment plans: a registered Phase 4 study evaluated patient satisfaction with overall face and neck appearance after combined treatment with onabotulinumtoxinA, Juvederm products, Kybella, CoolSculpting Elite and SkinMedica products in 130 participants, and another evaluated Juvederm products for overall facial appearance in 75 adults.[8][9]

For Juvederm fillers, reported effects include temporary redness, pain, swelling and bruising, and less commonly granulomas.[3] The manufacturer lists common Skinvive reactions as redness, lumps or bumps, swelling, bruising, pain, tenderness, firmness, discoloration and itching, most resolving within seven days, and less common reports of inflammation, nodules, allergic reaction, infection and abscess.[4]

The manufacturer's safety information says unintentional injection into a blood vessel is rare but can cause serious, possibly permanent complications including vision problems, blindness, stroke and scarring. It lists as contraindications a history of severe allergic reactions or anaphylaxis and allergy to lidocaine or to Gram-positive bacterial proteins, and states that safety in pregnancy, breastfeeding, people with a history of excessive scarring or pigmentation disorders, and in areas other than the cheeks has not been established.[4]

A laboratory study found that hyaluronidase can dissolve 22 commercial hyaluronic acid fillers, which is relevant to managing filler complications.[2] The manufacturer states the effectiveness of removing Skinvive has not been studied.[4]

In the pivotal trial, the announcement lists redness, lumps and bumps, swelling, bruising, tenderness, pain, firmness, discoloration and itching as the commonly reported reactions, mostly mild or moderate, with a few severe and rare cases lasting longer than 30 days. It adds that the label advises avoiding strenuous exercise, extensive sun or heat and alcohol for 24 hours after treatment, notes that blood thinners and aspirin may increase bruising, and says laser treatments or chemical peels afterward carry a risk of inflammation.[5]

A 2025 randomized, double-blind split-face trial in 25 women evaluated onabotulinumtoxinA combined with Juvederm Volite VYC-12 (Skinvive) for moderate and severe canthal lines, assessing efficacy, safety and durability.[1] A phase 3 trial of Juvederm Volite XC for neck lines enrolled 159 participants.[10] Other registered studies examine microdroplet hyaluronic acid on skin quality in people using GLP-1 agonists and satisfaction after jawline and neck treatment.[6][7]

timeline.event: Karl Meyer and John Palmer isolate hyaluronic acid and describe its role in skin.[3]
Hyaluronic acid first used for facial augmentation in Europe.[3]
Phase 3 trial of Juvederm Volite XC for neck lines begins.[10]
US FDA approves Skinvive by Juvederm to improve cheek skin smoothness in adults over 21 (announced 15 May).[5]
Split-face trial of botulinum toxin plus Skinvive published.[1]
